core_obligations: Prove (1): pick the submodule provided by the comparison lemma, use the degree bound for finite-length differences, and combine with the additivity statement to bound the degree of the discrepancy polynomial (proof lines 14458-14470).

Deduce (2) by comparing the degrees of the three polynomials through the estimate of (1), and get (3) from (2), the author leaving only the degenerate cases where one of the modules vanishes to the reader (proof lines 14470-14485).
proof_roadmap: Bound the discrepancy polynomial by the finite-length comparison (proof lines 14458-14470).
Read off the degrees in (2) and (3) (proof lines 14470-14486).
difficulty_reason: For a short exact sequence of finite modules over a Noetherian local ring the lemma bounds the discrepancy between the three Hilbert-Samuel functions in degree, identifies the maximum of the degrees of the outer two with the degree of the middle one, and transfers this to the associated dimension function (statement lines 14442-14456). The proof does not estimate each function separately: it chooses a submodule with finite length quotient, uses the degree bound for finite-length differences and additivity to bound the discrepancy, and then reads the degree statements off that bound (proof lines 14458-14486). Choosing the intermediate submodule so that the discrepancy becomes controlled is the content. H2.
